html:
Cuba is the largest island of the Caribbean, and a republic since 1902. The map shows it from 1914, but its history as Spanish Cuba goes back to 1511.

Under Spain, Havana was the meeting port of the treasure fleets. In the 1800s Cuba became the world's great sugar producer, with slavery lasting until 1886. Cubans fought two wars for independence, the second launched by José Martí in 1895. The United States stepped in during the Spanish-American War of 1898.

Independent Cuba stayed under the shadow of its neighbour:

  • The Platt Amendment let the United States intervene, and it kept a lease on Guantánamo Bay.
  • American companies owned much of the sugar industry.
  • Fulgencio Batista dominated politics from the 1930s and seized power in a coup in 1952.

The Cuban Revolution drove out Batista in 1959. Fidel Castro built a one-party socialist state allied with the Soviet Union. A failed American-backed invasion at the Bay of Pigs in 1961 was followed by the Cuban Missile Crisis of 1962, the closest the Cold War came to nuclear war.

The revolution brought free schools and health care, and also political prisons and exile; in the Mariel boatlift of 1980 over a hundred thousand Cubans left for Florida. When the Soviet Union fell, Cuba went through years of deep hardship. Raúl Castro succeeded his brother in 2008.
sum: Cuba is the largest island of the Caribbean, and a republic since 1902. The map shows it from 1914, but its history as Spanish Cuba goes back to 1511.
